new_entities.name: Pre-exercise caffeine intake
new_entities.description: Caffeine consumed before resistance exercise in ergogenic doses.

new_entities.name: Muscular strength
new_entities.description: Maximal force production during resistance exercise tasks.

edges.effect_quant: Acute pre-exercise caffeine produces a small but consistent improvement in maximal strength performance, even at relatively low doses.
edges.mechanism: Caffeine improves alertness, motor-unit recruitment, and perceived effort tolerance through adenosine-receptor antagonism rather than by changing muscle tissue directly. That mechanism fits the literature well: the strength benefit is usually measurable but modest, and strongest in acute performance settings rather than in long-term hypertrophy outcomes.
edges.summary: This is a real ergogenic edge, just not a dramatic one. Meta-analyses of resistance exercise studies consistently show that taking caffeine before lifting slightly improves maximal strength performance, with detectable benefit even at doses below the classic high-dose sports-supplement range.
edges.caveats: The average effect is small, and individual response varies with habitual caffeine use, dose, and the exercise tested. A positive pooled result does not mean every athlete or every session will show a clear practical benefit.

evidence.citation: Ferreira TT et al 2021 Crit Rev Food Sci Nutr
